attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, rebutting de Freitas. He is not quoting anyone else here.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: the historical point about anti-symbol neural-net enthusiasts and the 2022 point that red-cube/blue-cube descriptions still elude the state of the art. Says no more and no less than the post.

contract.note: An informed reader would take this plain reading: 'many' means a substantial strand, not all; 'elude' means not reliably handled, which fits the context; 'decades' means at least about twenty years. Hybrid work and one-off successes are rightly excluded as contradictions. Fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: 1997 SEP account, from before the post, describes radical connectionists who 'would eliminate symbolic processing'. A scholarly secondary source that establishes a substantial anti-symbolic strand.

The 2019 SEP revision still says many connectionists resist the implementational view, which carries the documentation past twenty years. It is a revision of the same account as e1, not an independent source.

Original DALL·E 2 paper, April 2022 (before May 14). It reports that unCLIP struggles to bind colors to the two cubes for 'a red cube on top of a blue cube'. This is direct evidence of unreliable compositional binding in a leading model.

reviews.rationale: Both parts hold. The SEP accounts (1997, 2019) document a long-standing anti-symbolic strand among connectionists. They also mention accommodating and hybrid camps, but that does not refute 'many'. The DALL·E 2 paper shows the leading 2022 model struggling with the exact red/blue cube binding prompt. Nothing in the packet shows reliable handling. The GLIDE comparison is relative only.
